extracted.intended_audience: people seeking grant funding (researchers, nonprofits, artists, grant writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and writing grant proposals to secure funding from governments, corporations, foundations, and trusts. Covers the overall grant-writing process, research and positioning of the proposal, typical proposal sections, submission, and post-award obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyzing the intended audience for the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyzing the intended audience for the proposal (listed as a core element of the proposal creation process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an analysis is necessary because the grant maker and recipient may not have completely similar interests; the writer should position the proposal to highlight aspects that fulfil the funder's needs. Grantsmanship analysis may involve conducting research on the organisation and corresponding with relevant staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyzing the purpose of the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyzing the purpose of the proposal (identify what the proposal intends to achieve).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifying purpose helps shape content, priorities, and how to present significance and outcomes to align with funder expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gathering information about the subject of the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Gathering information about the subject of the proposal (researching the project topic and context).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include literature review, data collection or projection; also includes researching funders and past awards (some agencies list recipients and titles online) and, in the U.S., requesting copies via the Freedom of Information Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing the proposal (composing the narrative and required materials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Involves creating a coherent proposal and positioning it to meet funder needs. Traditionally done by the applicant organization but third-party grant writers may be employed; drafting can be a team activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting the proposal (ensuring the proposal meets required format and presentation standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting is a distinct step of proposal creation—adhere to funder instructions for sections, length, and presentation to avoid desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revising, editing, and proofreading the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Revising, editing, and proofreading the proposal (iterative refinement of content and presentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These activities are overlapping and recursive with other steps; careful revision improves clarity, persuasiveness, and reduces errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting the proposal (final delivery of the application to the funder).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow submission instructions and deadlines closely; submission is the final stage of proposal creation before review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary or abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary or abstract (listed as an individual section of a grant proposal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a concise overview of the project—serves as the first impression for reviewers and may be used to assess fit quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction or narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction or narrative (the main descriptive section of a proposal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets context, frames the problem and approach, and leads into significance and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Mission statement (statement of the applicant's mission or organizational purpose).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies the applicant's goals and alignment with the proposed project and the funder's priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance (section articulating the importance of the proposed work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains why the project matters and what impact or contribution it will make; should be tailored to funder priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis (literature review, data collection or projection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis including literature review and data collection or projection (listed under 'Analysis').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates knowledge of the field, situates the project within existing work, and supports the project's rationale with data or projections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workplan
rubrics_metrics.description: Workplan (detailed plan of activities and timeline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlines tasks, milestones, responsibilities, and sequencing to show feasibility and realistic implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodology (methods to be used to carry out the project).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows rigor and appropriateness of methods for achieving objectives and producing the claimed outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation (how project success will be measured and assessed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe metrics, assessment methods, and processes for monitoring progress and measuring impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications (plans for disseminating results and communicating with stakeholders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain outreach, dissemination, and stakeholder communication strategies to demonstrate broader impact and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget (financial plan and justification for project costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, realistic cost estimates and justifications that align with proposed activities; follow funder formatting and allowable cost rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience (applicant and team qualifications and relevant track record).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document relevant past performance, expertise, and capacity to carry out the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices (supplementary materials attached to the proposal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include supporting documents such as CVs, letters of support, detailed methods or data that supplement the main narrative—ensure they conform to funder rules about appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post award phase / management and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Post award phase (the last part of the lifecycle of a grant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After funding is awarded, funders may require changes for continued support or as part of the grant contract; manage reporting, compliance, and any contractual obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research prior funded proposals and awardees
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate previous grant recipients and proposal titles (some agencies list recent recipients; FOIA requests possible in the U.S.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewing successful past proposals helps understand funder priorities and standards; use public lists or request documents where available to benchmark and model proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team drafting / collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Drafting in a team (some grant writers work in a team with other professionals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaboration can bring in subject-matter experts, budget specialists, and editors—coordinate roles, responsibilities, and integration of sections.
